## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvaraacchindana Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25) is a Vinaya text belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses the case of a Buddhist monk who gives robe-cloth to a fellow monk and subsequently reclaims it out of anger; committing this infraction entails forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the robe-cloth and formal confession (*pācittiya*) of the offense [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is shared extensively across early Buddhist monastic lineages [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25, Bhikkhu Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 25, and parallel nuns' rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Bi-Vb Np26) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Close Vinaya parallels exist in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions across diverse monastic schools, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with these transmissions, automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus align the text with Tibetan translations of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007), and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkā Vinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies over 600 shared formulaic passages across more than a hundred texts, exhibiting the largest overlaps in standard legal phrases with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3 and adjacent robe-related rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, such as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4, 5, 6, 10, and 20 [DharmaNexus].
